met_analysis:
The Depression over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal moved southeastwards with speed of 5 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 0530 hours IST of today, the 25th October, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 15.3°N and Longitude 91.2°E, about 440 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 880 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 980 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 1080 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1150 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh). It is very likely to move nearly southwards, intensify into a Deep Depression and then gradually recurve west-northwestwards over the Eastcentral & adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal today, the 25th October. Continuing to move west-northwestwards, it is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the Eastcentral & adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal by 26th October morning, and into a severe cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal around morning of 27th October, 2026. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach Westcentral Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around morning of 28th October, 2026. It is very likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.
The Low Pressure areaover Southeast Arabian sea and adjoining Lakshadweep area persisted over the same region at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 25th October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with Low Pressure areaover Southeast Arabian sea and adjoining Lakshadweep to north coastal Tamilnadu across Kerala extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists. Theupper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Bangladesh & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level persists with the trough aloft in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 74°E to the north of Lat. 28°N.
The induced upper cyclonic circulation over North Rajasthan & adjoining Haryana extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
